newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil futures end up $2.50, Brent off highs.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil futures end up $2.50, Brent off highs.

text.p: IPE gas oil ended up $2.50 a tonne on Tuesday at $172 on the September contract at the day's high.
Prices were boosted by strong Brent crude futures which climbed during the afternoon on news that Venezuela's main oil export shipping channel had been blocked.
October Brent was up 24 cents a barrel at $19.17 at 1632 GMT, having hit an intra-day high of $19.29 earlier.
A dredger went aground in the Lake Maracaibo shipping lane on Monday night, shutting the channel to tankers which normally export more than one million barrels of crude per day.
Brokers said gasoline had also buoyed the market and U.S. stock figures, due out later on Tuesday, would be important.
September NYMEX gasoline was up over one cent a gallon in early trading and stocks are running well below year ago levels.
Technical resistance on Brent was pegged by analysts at $19.29, the high from last Thursday and at $19.46 from a downtrend line.

Gains on gas oil futures were despite a sluggish physical market. Stocks of winter heating oil are well above year ago levels on both sides of the Atlantic and sellers are having to work harder than buyers to drum up interest. Prompt Rotterdam barges are at parity to the IPE, as are cargoes of Russian gas oil heading for Western buyers. --London newsroom, +44 171 542 4984
